chapter.title: The Application's Environment
chapter.para: An application that runs Rexx code decides what that code sees around it: the ADDRESS environments its commands go to, where its SAY writes and its PULL reads, which functions and VALUE selectors it has, and when it must stop. These are members of RexxInterpreter:

section.title: ADDRESS Environments
section.para: rexx.AddCommandEnvironment(name, handler) makes handler the environment name: ADDRESS name 'command' (or ADDRESS name, then 'command') calls it on the Rexx thread with a RexxCommand. Its result is RC (null: 0), whatever its sign: a negative RC raises nothing. A RexxCommandException raises ERROR, or FAILURE, with its RC and its message as condition("A"); a Rexx error of Rexx code that the handler called is raised again as itself; any other exception is SYNTAX 98.900, as a .NET error anywhere: ".NET error: Type: message", the exception in condition("O")~additional[2], its stack trace in [3]. Names are caseless; adding one again replaces its handler; a null handler is an ArgumentNullException. Each instance has its own environments, and every one takes ADDRESS ... WITH redirection: written without it, output and errors go to the console (Console.Out, Console.Error), as a program's would, and the write methods answer false.

rexx.RemoveCommandEnvironment(name) removes one (a name with no handler is an InvalidOperationException): ADDRESS name then raises FAILURE with RC 30, as for an environment that does not exist (ooRexx has no way to remove an environment: its entry stays, and answers so). Rexx code adds and removes them too, with and
(). These are the rules of the whole family of bridges (ooRexx/Python, ooRexx/Lua, ooRexx/JavaScript).

A RexxCommand (and a RexxFunctionCall, below) is valid only while its handler runs. Its indexer reads and sets the calling Rexx code's variables, their names as Rexx writes them, uppercased; setting null sets &nil; (Drop drops). The handler's own calls into Rexx (through Interpreter) run nested on the same thread.

example.title: An ADDRESS environment
example.screen: HELLO 42 0 2 1: a / 2: b ERROR 10 unknown command: nope

section.title: Standard Streams
section.para: Output, Error and Input are where the Rexx code's standard streams go, set at any time (or at creation, in RexxOptions):

listitem.para: SAY, LINEOUT and CHAROUT to the default stream, .output.
PULL, PARSE PULL, LINEIN and CHARIN from the default stream, .input. At its end, reads give "" and LINES() 0.

section.para: null is the process's own stream. What these do not catch, because it never passes through Rexx's streams: .stdout, .stderr and .stdin used directly, and the output of programs started by ADDRESS SYSTEM (which Rexx code can route itself: ADDRESS SYSTEM 'cmd' WITH OUTPUT USING (.output)).

Prefixes. What the Rexx code writes to the process's own streams carries BSF4ooRexx's prefixes, so that it stands out in the application's console or log: REXXout> (.output), REXXerr> (.error), REXXtrc> (.traceOutput, error messages too), and the prompts REXXin?> and REXXdbgIn?> before a line is read from .input or .debugInput. What goes to Output or Error, or comes from Input, has none. RexxOptions.StreamPrefixes = false, or rexx.StreamPrefixes = false at any time, turns them off; Rexx code changes one with .output~current~prefix = 'mine>' (or &nil;). A program run by rexx itself has none: its output is its own.

example.title: Standard streams and their prefixes
example.screen: REXXout>one REXXout>two REXXout>lines plain Name? Hello, ANN

section.title: Functions and VALUE Selectors
section.para: rexx.AddFunction(name, handler) gives the Rexx code a function, called as name(args) or CALL name args, on the Rexx thread. The handler is one of:

listitem.para: a Func<RexxFunctionCall, object?> (call => ...), which gets the call: its name, its arguments, the caller's variables; or an Action<RexxFunctionCall>, for a function with no result (fine for CALL; as a function, Rexx's error 44).

any delegate or method ((double a, double b) => Math.Sqrt(a * a + b * b)), whose parameters get the arguments converted by Rexx's rules (RexxConvert): a parameter with a default value may be left out, a params array takes the rest, and a parameter of type RexxFunctionCall gets the call.

section.para: The result goes to Rexx as any .NET value. A .NET exception is SYNTAX 40.900 (Incorrect call to routine) with its message; too few or too many arguments for a typed delegate, 40.3 and 40.4; an argument that does not convert, 40.900 naming it. The program's own routines and Rexx's built-in functions win over the application's; external functions of the same name (a library's, a file) are hidden by it. Names are caseless; adding one again replaces it.
section.programlisting: public sealed class RexxFunctionCall : RexxCallContext { public string Name { get; } // uppercased, unless called as a literal public IReadOnlyList<object?> Arguments { get; } // RexxString, RexxObject, a .NET object, null, RexxValue.Omitted public bool IsSubroutine { get; } // CALL name public T Arg<T>(int i, T fallback = default!); // from 0, by Rexx's rules }
section.para: rexx.AddValueSelector(selector, get, set) answers Rexx's VALUE(name, , selector) with get(name); VALUE(name, newValue, selector) answers get(name) and then calls set(name, newValue) (without a set, an error). The name is as the Rexx code gave it. Selectors are caseless; ooRexx's own (ENVIRONMENT) win. Functions and selectors need an instance made by Create: they use system exits, which ooRexx sets when an instance is created.

example.title: Functions and VALUE selectors of the application
example.screen: 5 Hello, Ann! Hola, Bob! VARS sees x = 42 blue red 40.3

section.title: Cancellation, Halt and Trace
section.para: Run, Run<T>, RunFile, RexxRoutine.Call and RexxObject.Send take a CancellationToken: when it is cancelled, the Rexx code that call runs is halted (a HALT condition, which it may trap), and the call throws OperationCanceledException, whose InnerException is the RexxException 4.1. Only that thread is halted. A token already cancelled stops the call before it starts (the same exception, with no inner one); one cancelled while a program or a routine is starting (Run, Call, RunFile) halts it at its first clause (unless the instance was created with ReliableCancellation false, : then it may be missed); one cancelled while the code is inside a command handler takes effect at the next clause. A method (Send) is halted only once its code runs: a token cancelled in the moment before that is missed.

Halt halts every Rexx thread of the instance. Trace sets Rexx's trace for the whole instance; it reaches only Rexx code running at that moment, so to trace one run, use the Rexx code's own TRACE (its output goes to Error).
